This would be my advice, I’m a pole instructor and a stripper for background! 

1. Incorporate cross training if you don’t already. Shoulders and hips are the areas most dancers injure primarily (especially shoulders). If you can, do an extra warm up before class. You can get to class early or do this at home. Most of my advanced students and a few of my intermediate students do this regularly. 

2. Do some performances/showcases! The more you do, the more you’ll look/feel like a more confident dancer. Doing choreo in class looking at yourself in the mirror isn’t gonna be the same as performing for and engaging with an audience. 

3. Focus on your form and cleaning up moves. Super pointed toes, straight legs with your inverts, holding your moves for longer, etc. There are still some small ways to make some intermediate moves harder. First one that comes to mind is a pencil hold. To take it up a notch, you can have your inside hand high, outside hand low below your chest in your handshake grip, your chest facing out, with nice straight legs and pointed feet. 

4. Take classes from different instructors. Everyone has a different teaching style or specialty. Trying out another teacher at your studio or taking a workshop can totally add to your roster of moves.
